source.result: Rune Heiremans, 5th place, World Championships 2026 (28 Aug 2026); the same 60 cards also took 6th (Satoshi Matsui). The best Nice result was 95th, so this Worlds list was used instead. It predates 30th Celebration but uses only cards that are still legal.
source.note: A real tournament list. card_text entries are short quotes from data/; see the full text there.

requirements: Real tournament list: a wall deck. Crustle takes no damage from Pokémon ex attacks, so ex-based decks can't Knock it Out; the rest of the deck heals, disrupts the opponent's hand and Energy, and wins slowly.

cards.name: Mega Kangaskhan ex
cards.role: Draw engine while Active and the main answer to single-Prize Pokémon that Crustle can't wall. Any Energy powers its attack.

cards.name: Dwebble
cards.role: Basic for Crustle; its 1-Energy attack searches the deck for Crustle and evolves into it right away.

cards.name: Crustle
cards.role: The wall: its Ability prevents all damage from attacks by Pokémon ex. Its attack ignores effects on the Defending Pokémon.

cards.name: Team Rocket's Petrel
cards.role: Searches any Trainer card: Eri, Boss's Orders, a Stadium or a heal, whatever the turn needs. Also triggers Team Rocket's Factory.

cards.name: Lillie's Determination
cards.role: Main draw Supporter.

cards.name: Boss's Orders
cards.role: Picks off support Pokémon and single-Prize threats. 4 copies because the deck wins by choosing which Pokémon to Knock Out.

cards.name: Eri
cards.role: Looks at the opponent's hand and discards up to 2 Items: removes their switching, search or Tool answers to Crustle.

cards.name: Hilda
cards.role: Finds an Evolution Pokémon and an Energy: Crustle plus its Energy in one card.

cards.name: Xerosic's Machinations
cards.role: The opponent discards down to 3 cards in hand.

cards.name: Pokémon Center Lady
cards.role: Heals 60 and removes Special Conditions.

cards.name: Jumbo Ice Cream
cards.role: Heals 80 from an Active Pokémon with 3+ Energy attached, keeping Kangaskhan or Crustle alive against single-Prize attackers.

cards.name: Pokégear 3.0
cards.role: Finds a Supporter from the top 7 cards. Limitless lists an older printing (sv01-186, G mark); this is the legal printing in your data.

cards.name: Buddy-Buddy Poffin
cards.role: Benches 2 Dwebble on turn 1.

cards.name: Special Red Card
cards.role: Late-game hand disruption.

cards.name: Switch
cards.role: Moves a damaged or stuck Pokémon to the Bench.

cards.name: Ultra Ball
cards.role: Searches any Pokémon.

cards.name: Enhanced Hammer
cards.role: Discards an opponent's Special Energy.

cards.name: Handheld Fan
cards.role: Tool: when the Active holder is damaged, an Energy moves off the attacker onto the opponent's Bench, slowing their next attack.

cards.name: Hero's Cape
cards.role: ACE SPEC Tool: +100 HP.

cards.name: Lumiose City
cards.role: Stadium: once a turn either player may bench a Basic from their deck, but that turn ends. Benches Dwebble when there's nothing to attack with, and the opponent can use it too. 1 copy.

cards.name: Festival Grounds
cards.role: Stadium: Pokémon with Energy attached are immune to Special Conditions, protecting the wall from poison and confusion.

cards.name: Team Rocket's Factory
cards.role: Stadium: draw 2 after playing a Team Rocket Supporter, which turns every Petrel into search plus draw.

cards.name: Growing Grass Energy
cards.role: Provides Grass and gives the Grass Pokémon it is attached to +20 HP.

cards.name: Mist Energy
cards.role: Blocks the effects of opposing attacks on the Pokémon it is attached to, so Crustle can't be pushed aside or disabled.

cards.name: Spiky Energy
cards.role: Provides Colorless and punishes an attacker that damages the Active Pokémon it is attached to.

cards.name: Grass Energy
cards.role: Basic Grass Energy for Crustle and for Hilda to find.

strategy: Get Crustle into play fast (Dwebble can evolve itself from the deck) and make the opponent attack it. Decks that rely on Pokémon ex can't damage it at all, so they run out of attackers while Crustle chips away. Mega Kangaskhan ex draws cards and handles single-Prize Pokémon, healed by Jumbo Ice Cream. Eri, Xerosic's Machinations and Special Red Card strip the opponent's hand, Enhanced Hammer and Handheld Fan slow their Energy, Boss's Orders picks the targets, and Petrel finds whichever piece is needed.

main_resource.resource: How many hits from Pokémon that are not ex Crustle survives (ex attacks do 0 damage to it)
main_resource.formula: Crustle has 150 HP: 170 with Growing Grass Energy, 270 with Hero's Cape too. A 120-damage non-ex attacker needs 2 hits on 170 HP and 3 hits on 270 HP. With a Jumbo Ice Cream (-80) between every hit, that becomes 3 and 5 hits.

cards.name: Growing Grass Energy
cards.effect: +20 HP on a Grass Pokémon (4 copies)

cards.name: Jumbo Ice Cream
cards.effect: -80 damage a turn; Crustle's attack costs exactly the 3 Energy it needs (4 copies)

cards.name: Spiky Energy
cards.effect: puts 2 damage counters (20) on every attacker that damages the Active Pokémon

cards.name: Handheld Fan
cards.effect: moves an Energy off the attacker, so its next attack is delayed

cards.name: Mist Energy
cards.effect: blocks attack effects on its Pokémon (damage is not an effect)

cards.name: Switch
cards.effect: moves a damaged Crustle out; its Retreat Cost is 3

card_text: Crustle: "Prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from your opponent's Pokémon ex."
Growing Grass Energy: "The {G} Pokémon this card is attached to gets +20 HP."
Hero's Cape: "The Pokémon this card is attached to gets +100 HP."
Mist Energy: "Prevent all effects of attacks used by your opponent's Pokémon done to the Pokémon this card is attached to." ... "Damage is not an effect."
Festival Grounds: "can't be affected by any Special Conditions"
synergies.how_they_interact: Crustle is a wall only against Pokémon ex. Mist Energy and Festival Grounds close the other ways through it: effects such as confusion or being stopped from retreating. Together the Energy and Cape give it 270 HP. Limits: the wall does nothing against attackers that are not ex, Mist Energy doesn't stop damage, and Festival Grounds protects the opponent's Pokémon that have Energy too.

card_text: Crustle: "Superb Scissors"
Jumbo Ice Cream: "Heal 80 damage from your Active Pokémon that has 3 or more Energy attached."
Pokémon Center Lady: "Heal 60 damage from 1 of your Pokémon, and it recovers from all Special Conditions."
Spiky Energy: "put 2 damage counters on the Attacking Pokémon"
Handheld Fan: "move an Energy from the Attacking Pokémon to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon"
synergies.how_they_interact: The answer to attackers that are not ex. Crustle's attack costs Grass + 2 Colorless, which is exactly the 3 Energy Jumbo Ice Cream asks for, so the Crustle that attacks every turn also qualifies for 4 Ice Creams. Each hit on it also returns 20 with Spiky Energy and can pull an Energy off the attacker with Handheld Fan. Against a 120-damage attacker, a Crustle with Hero's Cape and an Ice Cream every turn takes 5 hits, and the attacker loses 20 HP and an Energy along the way. Switch is the only free way out when Crustle (Retreat 3) has to leave.

card_text: Dwebble: "Search your deck for a card that evolves from this Pokémon and put it onto this Pokémon to evolve it."
Hilda: "Search your deck for an Evolution Pokémon and an Energy card"
Buddy-Buddy Poffin: "Search your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon with 70 HP or less"
Lumiose City: "that player may search their deck for a Basic Pokémon and put it onto their Bench" ... "their turn ends"
synergies.how_they_interact: Three independent ways to have Crustle in play by turn 2-3. Poffin benches 2 Dwebble (70 HP fits) and Dwebble's attack puts Crustle on itself straight from the deck for 1 Energy, no Stage 1 card in hand needed. Hilda adds Crustle and an Energy in one card, and Ultra Ball finds either. Lumiose City benches a Basic from the deck once a turn but ends your turn, so use it only when you have no attack to make; the opponent can use it too. Limit: Dwebble must be Active with an Energy to use Ascension.

card_text: Team Rocket's Petrel: "Search your deck for a Trainer card"
Team Rocket's Factory: "if they played a Supporter card that has "Team Rocket" in its name from their hand this turn, they may draw 2 cards"
Pokégear 3.0: "Look at the top 7 cards of your deck. You may reveal a Supporter card you find there"
Lillie's Determination: "draw 6 cards. If you have exactly 6 Prize cards remaining, draw 8 cards instead."
Mega Kangaskhan ex: "Draw 2 cards."
synergies.how_they_interact: 19 Supporters and only 1 can be played a turn, so the search cards decide which one. Petrel finds whichever Trainer the board needs (Eri, Boss's Orders, Jumbo Ice Cream, a Stadium), and with Factory in play it also draws 2. Pokégear 3.0 reaches the Supporter from the top 7. Lillie's draws 8 only at 6 Prizes, so play it early. Mega Kangaskhan ex draws 2 more while Active, and Boss's Orders gives it the single-Prize target to Knock Out; it is a 2-Prize Pokémon outside Crustle's wall.

card_text: Eri: "Your opponent reveals their hand, and you discard up to 2 Item cards you find there."
Xerosic's Machinations: "Your opponent discards cards from their hand until they have 3 cards in their hand."
Special Red Card: "You can use this card only if your opponent has 3 or fewer Prize cards remaining." ... "Your opponent shuffles their hand and puts it on the bottom of their deck."
Enhanced Hammer: "Discard a Special Energy from 1 of your opponent's Pokémon."
synergies.how_they_interact: A wall wins by making the opponent run out of answers while Crustle chips with 120 a turn. Eri strips up to 2 Items (their switching and search) from the revealed hand, Xerosic's cuts it to 3, Special Red Card resets it at 3 or fewer Prizes (an Item, so it can follow a Supporter in the same turn), and Enhanced Hammer takes a Special Energy off. Boss's Orders then pulls out the support Pokémon that is not ex. Only one of Eri or Xerosic's per turn, so choose by the hand size Eri reveals or Petrel finds.
